_what: MY READING. A hand join of the 32 `checked_by` statements to the 114 registry conventions, made by reading both. It is NOT mechanical and must never be quoted as if it were. Every pairing carries a confidence I assigned; `registry` [] means I could find no entry the statement corresponds to, which is itself a finding.
_confidence: high = the statement and the entry state the same claim in near-identical words; medium = the same underlying fact, differently scoped or worded; low = adjacent, and a reader could reasonably disagree.

statements.text: cross-staff measure count: every staff of a system prints the SAME number of bars
statements.note: No entry states the bar-count equality itself. C56 (a barline runs the FULL HEIGHT of its system) is the convention it follows FROM, not the claim.

statements.text: a systemic barline crosses every staff of the system at one x
the count may not EXCEED the work roster
statements.note: NOT AN ENGRAVING CONVENTION. The roster is a CATALOG fact (source_kind catalog), deliberately independent of the plate. The registry describes ink and correctly holds nothing for it.

statements.text: across systems of one page the count is equal, or a subset explained by tacet staves
cross-staff measure count agreement (measure_count_warning)
statements.note: same gap as CB01

statements.text: a merged bar sums to a MULTIPLE of the meter; a split bar to a fraction
statements.note: THE BAR SUM HAS NO REGISTRY ENTRY. See FINDINGS §5.

statements.text: staves of one bracket group are one instrument FAMILY
statements.note: ⚠️ C59 CONTRADICTS IT IN TERMS: 'A bracket BLOCK is an engraving unit, not an instrument family.' The declaration asserts what a MEASURED entry denies.

statements.text: roster membership: an instrument the work is not scored for is IMPOSSIBLE
statements.note: catalog fact, as CB03

statements.text: label contradiction: a staff whose OWN margin label was read on THIS page, named something else
statements.note: C71 is the nearest ('an engraver does not name one section with two different abbreviations on ONE system') but is about two LABELS, not label-vs-assignment.

statements.text: the implied written range must contain this staff's own positions under its clef
statements.note: an INSTRUMENT fact, not an engraving one. Same for CB15 and CB23.

statements.text: a slot's instrument is the SAME on every system it appears on
label contradiction, at slot scope
statements.note: as CB09

statements.text: the part count may not exceed the work roster
statements.note: catalog fact, as CB03

statements.text: each part carries ONE instrument across every system it appears on
implied pitches must fall in the instrument's written range
statements.note: instrument fact, as CB10

statements.text: the glyph stands ON this staff (a measure cell is the staff plus four staff spaces of air)
statements.note: The CELL PADDING is ours, not an engraving convention; C5 is the engraving fact that makes the padding necessary and L2 the registration rule the test rests on.

statements.text: key-signature slot fit: the measured accidental RUN fits this candidate's slot table and not another's
continuity: a part's clef is stable across systems unless a change is printed
the accidental ORDER is fixed: a run that SKIPS a slot is impossible
across the staves of a system the DELTA is shared, never the value -- transposing parts print different signatures for one key
statements.note: No entry states the transposition-delta rule. C81+L39 (timpani/horns/trumpets print NO key signature) is adjacent and is not it.

statements.text: a key CHANGE is printed on every staff at the same bar
a spurious or missing notehead breaks the OWNING bar's duration sum
statements.note: bar sum, see FINDINGS §5

statements.text: the owned glyph's implied pitch must fall in the owner's written range
statements.note: instrument fact, as CB10

statements.text: a TIE joins two heads of the SAME staff step
of two arcs STACKED over the same notes the lower is a tie and the upper a slur
statements.note: the registry entry IS this statement -- both are Sean's S6

statements.text: bar sum: the durations of one voice in one bar must equal the meter
statements.note: bar sum, see FINDINGS §5

statements.text: bar sum: a wrong ratio breaks it
statements.note: bar sum, see FINDINGS §5

statements.text: the group must hold exactly as many notes as the digit claims
statements.note: C54 states WHERE the digit and bracket are printed, not that the member count must match the digit. The count claim may have no entry.

statements.text: the bar sum: one event contributes ONE duration
statements.note: bar sum, see FINDINGS §5

statements.text: bar sum, on every bar of every staff it governs
statements.note: bar sum, see FINDINGS §5

statements.text: a meter is a SYSTEM fact: a mid-staff change no other staff witnessed is a misread
a column is an instant
statements.note: the registry entry IS this statement
